profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 82 (Alco Properties missing-address campaign): confirmed this rows identity as the historic Pittock Block building in downtown Portland, housing a NWAX Point of Presence internet exchange, via Wikipedia. Applied 921 Southwest Washington Street from a reverse geocode of this rows own coordinates whose street name independently matches Wikipedias named block boundary. The earlier domain-mismatch flag for pittock.com stands unresolved.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] An earlier pass on file for this Portland, Oregon row flagged that the operators domain, pittock.com, resolves to an unrelated third party blog rather than any data center or exchange page, and could not locate the operators current web presence. This session did not find a working Alco Properties or Pittock branded site either, that flag stands. This session did confirm the underlying facility itself independently, however. The Pittock Block, a National Register of Historic Places listed building built in 1913 on the former site of publisher Henry L. Pittocks home, occupying a city block between Southwest 9th and 10th Avenues and Southwest Stark and Washington Streets in downtown Portland, per Wikipedia houses a NWAX point of presence, also called the Portland NAP, serving as Portlands Internet exchange point, alongside tenants including the City Club of Portland and the Oregon Symphonys administrative offices. This matches this registry rows own name, the Pittock Internet Exchange. Reverse geocoding this rows own stored coordinates through a third party service returned 921 Southwest Washington Street, Portland, OR 97205 at 0.9 confidence, whose street name independently matches one of the four boundary streets Wikipedia names for the Pittock Block, corroborating the street and block placement, though the specific house number comes from the geocoder alone and is not independently confirmed. This session applies that address given this convergence. The operating internet exchange organizations own site gives only a separate administrative or headquarters address in a different part of the Portland area, not specifically this downtown peering location, so that address is not applied here.

reading: Alco Properties is a Portland, Oregon commercial real estate and property management company whose portfolio includes the Pittock Block Building at 921 SW Washington Street, historically known in the data center and networking industry as the Pittock Internet Exchange. The building functions as a carrier hotel and peering point in downtown Portland, a role documented by third-party data center directories rather than by Alco's own materials, which focus on property management and leasing rather than technical infrastructure. Because Alco Properties' public-facing presence is oriented toward real estate services rather than colocation or wholesale data center marketing, this registry could not verify founding year, capacity in megawatts, or a tenant list directly from the operator, and records the facility's data center function as sourced from trade directories rather than the operator's own publications. This pattern, a legacy commercial building whose internet exchange function was established informally over time rather than through a purpose-built data center brand, is common among older peering locations in secondary markets and distinguishes Alco from the purpose-built wholesale and hyperscale developers elsewhere in this registry.
